review_comments:
The way this is written is going to be wrong near the key gradient points, especially noticeably near the last one (due to the discontinuity in colours at 8*). Because this is doing `point >= endStop.position`, it is assuming that the star rating should be *truncated* to two decimal places. While in fact in most places that use `.ToString()` to display it numerically it is being *rounded* to two decimal places.

This means that if I have a map that has, say, 7.9996*, it will show as 8.00* in text, but still have the background colour of 7.99*. I've even found a map where this happens without looking very hard at all:

![osu_2021-08-03_23-29-00](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/128088775-3ef4c2ad-5781-47ff-94ff-311e2065bd18.jpg)

It's nigh-unreadable, because `StarRatingDisplay` doesn't use orange-1 foreground colour correctly above 6.50* as noted in the other comment, but the text says 8.00*, yet the background colour is not black.

The proper way to do this would be to apply tolerance of 0.005* (half the "tick").
Unexpected case there, but good find.
I've went for `Math.Round(starDifficulty, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)` to perfectly match `.ToString("0.00")` for the time being.
~~Yeah... I'm interested to hear the other's opinions on having gamma correction in `Interpolation.ValueAt(Color4)` itself, as that'll likely benefit colour transitions in general I believe.~~

I'm confused. How is interpolation done in the SRGB space? That would mean the input colours are coming in as SRGB (are they?)
As it is, doesn't this mean the following process is taking place?:
```
input colour (linear)
SampleFromLinearGradient() -> (assumes SRGB) .ToLinear() -> return colour
Drawable.Colour = colour -> implicit conversion from Color4 to SRGColour -> (assumes SRGB) .ToLinear()
```
So there are two from-SRGB conversions taking place after the above patch, and one from-SRGB conversion taking place in the original changes.
Isn't the issue instead that this function doesn't output an SRGB colour? That is, changing to `return Interpolation.ValueAt(...).ToSRGB()`.

I'll admit that I didn't 100% confirm what was going on, just wrote what would make sense to me and compared output, but if the source hex colours were taken from figma, then those would be srgb, right? Hence the first two conversions.
In that case then I'd expect the `.ToLinear()` to be done locally where those colours are declared.

Are you getting the values from the figma parameter display, or using an eye-dropper? I think these may give different values. I would presume the parameters listed would give the original values, right? We should never actually be using SRGB post conversion values.

I have always been using the figma parameter display, and now after reading a bit on the sRGB/linear (hard-to-grasp) logic, the interpolation should be done in the linear space? unless the colours provided by figma are in the sRGB space...?
@arflyte can you confirm whether the figma colours are sRGB? I’ve thought they were in the standard RGB colour space until now.

Relevant docs: https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039825114-Color-management-in-the-desktop-app

> In the browser, Figma uses a managed sRGB color profile.

This is likely because the web at large also uses sRGB, so for the colours to match it only makes sense to do that for the CSS rules.

@smoogipoo I'm not sure what the "standard RGB space" would mean in this context? I don't think anything of the sort exists? There's no possible RGB gamut that encompasses all possible human-perceptible colours (at least not one without negative coefficients, if you include CIE RGB in that). sRGB is the "safe" colour profile as most everything should support it.

> @arflyte can you confirm whether the figma colours are sRGB? I’ve thought they were in the standard RGB colour space until now.

I already went through this with flyte since he used to have his figma and photoshop set wrong. You can only assume all colours are in sRGB for all provided designs or nothing will make sense.

The code above by @bdach looks to be correct in what we want here.
Right, one remaining question I have is whether we can have the proposed logic in `Interpolation.ValueAt(Color4)` itself? assuming that the input should always be in the sRGB space.
For now that is the safe and simple assumption if we are aiming to match web colours, yes.
